Pressetext  ·  Press release

Beton Galerie is pleased to present Halbinsel / Peninsula, the first solo exhibition by the Norwegian sculptor Solveig Tarkamp (b. 1981, Tromsø; lives Oslo and Berlin) at the gallery. The exhibition gathers fourteen new works in polished basalt, raw sea-salt, and cold projected light, made over an eighteen-month research period across the Varanger Peninsula and at the Niederfinow basalt quarry in northeastern Brandenburg.

Tarkamp's practice has, for more than a decade, taken as its central subject the geological time-scale of stone and the human duration spent in its company. The works in Halbinsel / Peninsula refuse a clean distinction between site and gallery, sample and sculpture, the quarry and the white cube — echoing, but never simply rehearsing, Robert Smithson's site–nonsite dialectic. Where Smithson catalogued a fragment in order to point back to its origin, Tarkamp insists that the basalt block on the gallery floor is the peninsula, materially continuous with it: salt of the same sea has been carried by hand to the same stone, here, in another room.

The exhibition is organised as a slow procession through three temperatures. The first room (Hauptraum) presents the Silt series — six polished basalt forms of varying scale, the largest, Untitled (silt iv), 2025, measuring 142 × 80 × 60 cm and weighing approximately 740 kg. These have been cut against the grain of the columnar basalt and worked by hand over many months until the surface achieves what Tarkamp calls "a wetness without water" — a quality of polish that registers the smallest changes in ambient light. The floor between them is strewn with twelve kilograms of unwashed Varanger sea-salt, swept loosely each morning by the gallery staff according to a written protocol provided by the artist.

In the adjoining Saal, the projection works of the Peninsula series take over. Here Tarkamp deploys a single 4000 K LED line projector — a colour temperature she associates with the noon light of the polar coast in February — to rake low across two slate panels and the bare concrete floor. The work Peninsula (March, 7:42), 2026, programmes a fourteen-minute slow drift in luminance corresponding to a documented sunrise observed by the artist on 11 March 2025; in Peninsula (October, 16:08), 2026, the same equipment performs the opposite gesture, a long descent into red. One thinks here, perhaps inevitably, of Hilma af Klint's serial light, or of Tacita Dean's projector works, but Tarkamp's interest is more austere and more local: she wants the room itself to become, briefly, the latitude she has measured.

The Project Room downstairs is given over to the artist's continuing Notation series: hand-cut paper scores, each describing in pencil and graphite the path of a single morning walked along the Varanger coast. Eight new Notations are installed here, pinned directly to the wall with brass tacks and left unframed. The drawings make no claim to representation — they are protocols for being in a place — and yet, in their accumulation, a peninsula does in fact begin to appear.

Tarkamp is the recipient of the Lorck Schive Kunstpris (2022) and the Henie Onstad Sculpture Prize (2024); her work is held in the collections of Astrup Fearnley Museet, Oslo; Henie Onstad Kunstsenter, Høvikodden; and the Sammlung Marx, Berlin. Halbinsel / Peninsula is her first institutional-scale solo presentation in Germany and the gallery's most ambitious sculpture exhibition to date. A bilingual publication — designed by the studio HelloMe, with essays by the curator and the geographer Hilde Storaas — is released on the occasion of the exhibition.

The exhibition is accompanied by a programme of three public events: an artist talk between Solveig Tarkamp and the curator on 25 April, a curator's tour with Karim Behzadi on 13 June, and a one-evening performance by the composer Lina Solberg using basalt percussion and field recordings made on the peninsula, on 9 July. Details below.

— Text: Karim Behzadi, Senior Curator. Berlin, April 2026.

The Artist

Solveig Tarkamp (b. 1981, Tromsø, Norway) lives and works between Oslo and Berlin. She studied at the Kunstakademiet i Oslo (MFA, 2008) and at the Städelschule, Frankfurt (Meisterschülerin under Tobias Rehberger, 2010).

Her practice is grounded in extended residencies in arctic and subarctic landscapes and an ongoing collaboration with the Niederfinow basalt quarry, where she has worked since 2017. The exhibition Halbinsel / Peninsula is her first solo presentation with Beton Galerie.

Tarkamp has exhibited at Astrup Fearnley Museet (2024), Kunsthalle Bern (2022), and the 14th Lyon Biennale (2017). She is the recipient of the Lorck Schive Kunstpris and the Henie Onstad Sculpture Prize.

Related programming

Free with admission · Reservation recommended

Saturday 25 April · 18:00

Artist talk:
Solveig Tarkamp im Gespräch mit Karim Behzadi

The artist and curator discuss the eighteen-month research period behind Halbinsel / Peninsula and the long collaboration with the Niederfinow basalt quarry. In English, with simultaneous translation into German.

Hauptraum · 60 minutes, followed by drinks

Saturday 13 June · 16:00

Curator's tour with Karim Behzadi

A walk-through of the exhibition with the curator, focusing on the relationship between the Silt sculptures and the Peninsula projection works, and the long history of land-art reference behind the artist's practice.

Meet at the front desk · 45 minutes · DE / EN

Thursday 9 July · 20:30

Performance program:
Lina Solberg, basalt / lyd

A one-evening live performance by the Trondheim-based composer Lina Solberg, using basalt percussion, contact microphones, and field recordings made on the Varanger Peninsula during the artist's residency. Limited capacity.

Saal · Doors 20:00 · 40 minutes · Reservation required

Anlässlich der Ausstellung erschienen

On the occasion of the exhibition, a publication is released:
Solveig Tarkamp — Halbinsel / Peninsula

A bilingual (DE / EN) clothbound monograph of 248 pages, with newly commissioned essays by Karim Behzadi and the geographer Hilde Storaas, an extended studio conversation with the artist, and full documentation of all fourteen works. The publication includes archival images from Tarkamp's Varanger residency, 2024–2025.
